# NSCH K2Q31A Baseline — Experiment Report (`NSCH_EXPERIMENT_REPORT.md`)

**Experiment:** NSCH-K2Q31A-BASELINE-v1 · **Frozen:** 2026-10-20T17:03:43+00:00 · **Evaluated on 2025:** 2026-10-20T17:04:38+00:00  
*Generated by `python -m nsch_baseline.evaluate`; numbers are copied from the saved metric files.*

> The outcome is K2Q31A: whether a PARENT REPORTS that a doctor or other health care provider has EVER told them the child has ADD/ADHD (US survey data, 2023-2025). This is not a clinical diagnosis, not an ADHD presentation, and not a prediction about any real MathQuest learner. Research demonstration only. Not a diagnostic model, not an ADHD presentation classifier, not a longitudinal or learning-readiness predictor, and not approved for integration into MathQuest.

## Data and design

| Partition | Years | n | Positives | Prevalence |
| :--- | :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Training | 2023–2024 | 20,104 | — | 14.2 % |
| Validation | 2023–2024 | 5,027 | 714 | 14.2 % |
| **Held-out test** | **2025** | 10,743 | 1,634 | 15.2 % |

Children aged 6–10 with a valid K2Q31A answer. Split stratified by year × target, seed 20261021. 74 conservative Tier A features (277 encoded columns); no survey weights or year used as predictors. The 2025 file was not opened during training, model selection or threshold setting.

| random_forest | `{"n_estimators": 300, "min_samples_leaf": 30, "max_features": "sqrt"}` | 0.6993 | 0.3030 | 0.1136 |
| random_forest | `{"n_estimators": 300, "min_samples_leaf": 60, "max_features": "sqrt"}` | 0.6962 | 0.3020 | 0.1141 |

**Selected:** logistic_regression `{"C": 0.1}` — highest validation ROC-AUC (4 d.p.), then lowest validation Brier. Decision threshold **0.1259** (maximises Youden's J (sensitivity + specificity - 1) on the validation partition).

## Interpretation and limitations

- 2025 ROC-AUC (0.736) is slightly higher than validation (0.709). The pipeline and features were frozen before 2025 was opened, so this is not tuning to the test year; it reflects sampling variation and differences in the 2025 sample composition (higher prevalence, different state mix). The provisional intervals should be read before drawing conclusions from the difference.
- Discrimination is **modest** (ROC-AUC 0.74); the model ranks children better than chance but many children with reported ADHD history receive low scores and most flagged children have no reported history (see precision). This is expected: only stable/contextual features are used, by design, to avoid target leakage.
- One threshold for everyone produces very different error profiles by subgroup (see the table: e.g. boys receive higher scores, giving higher sensitivity but much lower specificity than girls). This mirrors the higher reported prevalence in boys and must not be read as a property of individual children.
- Missingness is informative: blank answers form their own category, and item non-response is associated with the outcome. Inputs with many missing values are therefore not representative (the demo warns about this).
- The outcome is parent-reported 'ever told', not a verified diagnosis, and reflects access to care, insurance, state and reporting practices as well as the child.
- Cross-sectional survey: no feature can be shown to precede the outcome; associations are not causal.
- Official codebook (special missing codes) and survey-design guidance were not available; missing values of different kinds are pooled, and all uncertainty estimates are provisional and not design-adjusted.
- Metrics are unweighted (sample, not US population). US-only data; no transfer to Sri Lankan children.
- Not for individual use; not integrated into MathQuest.

## Reproduce

```
cd research/recommendation_engine/ml_experiments
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m nsch_baseline.train      # 2023-2024 only; freezes the model
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m nsch_baseline.evaluate   # one evaluation on 2025; writes this report
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m nsch_baseline.demo       # prediction + SHAP for one held-out example
```

Library versions: `{"python": "3.13.14", "scikit-learn": "1.9.1", "pandas": "3.0.6", "numpy": "2.5.4", "joblib": "1.6.0", "shap": "0.54.1"}`
